subject.title: fix: CLI commands hang while checking large state databases

question: Should ordinary CLI bootstrap be allowed to defer unrelated current-schema database corruption to explicit Doctor/full-verification paths in exchange for avoiding repeated full scans on large healthy databases?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes the product boundary for when existing state corruption is detected and surfaced. Tests show the branch preserves full Doctor detection, but only maintainers can decide whether ordinary commands should continue to discover those defects automatically.

options.title: Accept scoped CLI preflight
options.body: Land the responsiveness improvement with the documented contract that explicit Doctor and migration-owner paths remain responsible for full-database integrity detection.

options.title: Keep automatic full detection
options.body: Retain the prior full integrity scan for ordinary CLI bootstrap so every command continues to surface unrelated corruption immediately, accepting the startup cost.

options.title: Add visible escalation
options.body: Keep the scoped gate but add a clear command-level warning or recovery path when conditions suggest users should run full Doctor verification.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped CLI preflight
recommendation.body: Land the responsiveness improvement with the documented contract that explicit Doctor and migration-owner paths remain responsible for full-database integrity detection.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review identified the key correctness boundary that the latest head changes, making them the strongest available routing candidate from the supplied evidence.
